claims.source_quote_ar: مجيء النفي على هذا السنن المتلو بديع
claims.claim_ar: مجيء النفي على هذا السنن المتلو بديع في صيغة النفي والتصريح بكونهم ليسوا بشركاء — بديع بلاغي في ترتيب النفي والتوكيد.
claims.claim_en: The placement of the negation in this successive pattern is rhetorically novel ('badi'): the arrangement of negation and affirmation enhances eloquence and forcefully negates that they are partners with God.
claims.rhetorical_effect: strengthens the denial by a striking, artful placement of the negative, increasing impact on the listener.

claims.claim_ar: افتتاح بالخطاب الإلهي بـ«قُلْ» كأمر إلهي موجّه إلى الرسول للبيان والتوبيخ — أسلوب حكيم وتعليمي.
claims.claim_en: The imperative 'قُلْ' opens the address as a divine command directing the Prophet to speak; a didactic, authoritative rhetorical style (aslūb ḥakīm).
claims.rhetorical_effect: gives the statement authoritative force and frames the subsequent reproach as divinely sanctioned speech.

claims.claim_ar: المزاوجة بين الظاهر والباطن (ما ظهر وما بطن) كإيحاء شامل لنفي الأفعال الظاهرة والسريرة — تركيب تبايقي وتوكيدي.
claims.claim_en: The pairing of outward and inward (apparent and hidden) acts is a balancing/antithetical device (tibāq), encompassing both visible and concealed sins and thereby broadening the prohibition's scope.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting commentary uses the term ظاهِر/ظاهرِه but does not verbatim quote the exact phrase 'ما ظهر وما بطن' from the verse; the mapping to tibāq (pairing) is inferred.
claims.rhetorical_effect: extends the prohibition to both external acts and internal intent, increasing moral comprehensiveness and psychological pressure.

warnings: Claims are based on the provided commentary chunks; some mappings (e.g., assigning 'tibaq' to the verse's ظاهر/باطن pairing) are inferential where the chunk uses related vocabulary but not the exact verse wording—see needs_review_reason on that claim.
